endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: along with a detailed assessment of the issue and proposed remediation plan;

endorsements.title: FUTURE-AI: international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable artificial intelligence in healthcare
endorsements.quote: Mitigation measures might include warnings to the users, system shutdown, reprocessing of the input data, the acquisition of new input data, or the use of an alternative procedure or human judgment only.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Use organizational risk tolerance to evaluate acceptable risks and performance metrics and decommission or retrain pre-trained models that perform outside of defined limits.

endorsements.title: Health Equity Across the AI Lifecycle (HEAAL) framework
endorsements.issuer: Health AI Partnership; PLOS Digital Health (PMID 38723025, doi:10.1371/journal.pdig.0000390)
endorsements.quote: If the monitoring results diverge from these objectives, the AI solution undergoes either updates or decommissioning.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Additionally, a process should be in place to detect patterns of patient harm associated with a given AI model and report harms to the developer team, and a process should be in place for determining if the Al should continue to operate, needs to be refined, or should be sunsetted in the event of safety issues and/or poor outcomes.

endorsements.title: Artificial intelligence in traumatic stress treatment: The TRUST framework for ethical development, clinical applications, and research advancement
endorsements.quote: Postdeployment strategies include mandating adverse event reporting systems with close oversight, conducting ongoing bias testing across diverse user groups, tracking emerging evidence and updating algorithms to align with new evidence, and performing deimplementation strategies when harms or risks are detected ( Labkoff et al., 2024 ).

commentary.bottom_line: Six frameworks and guidance documents endorse a process for deciding whether underperforming AI continues, is remediated or retrained, or is decommissioned, but no supplied study tests such a process or measures how often the hazard occurs. Health systems that adopt this recommendation would be acting on expert consensus rather than on outcome evidence.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. The six sources are frameworks, guidance, and one commentary, which express consensus rather than measured effects. Under GRADE conventions, certainty about whether a disposition process improves safety or outcomes cannot be rated, because no study informs it.

Endorsement strength varies across sources. One CHAI playbook states the practice as a must, CHAI's assurance guide, NIST AI 600-1, and the TRUST commentary use should, FUTURE-AI uses may, and HEAAL describes it. NIST ties decommissioning or retraining to performance outside defined organizational risk limits, which gives administrators a documented threshold approach to cite.

commentary.research_gap: No study compares health systems or AI deployments with and without a structured continue, remediate, or decommission process. Studies are needed that measure how long underperforming tools stay in use, how often disposition decisions are made, what thresholds trigger them, and whether patient harm or performance changes after remediation or retirement.
commentary.underserved_note: No supplied study tested the practice in any population, so there is no evidence on whether a disposition process works for Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy patients. The HEAAL framework frames decommissioning around equity objectives, but that is guidance, and whether disposition decisions account for subgroup performance remains untested.
